text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 2.3% today as oil prices surged on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Brent crude topped $103 a barrel after reports that the U.S. is preparing for possible large-scale military operations in Iran, which raises the risk of supply disruptions. For a refiner, higher crude costs can squeeze margins, but the company is also benefiting from the jump in energy prices themselves and from refineries operating at 92.7% capacity—near full steam—which helps absorb input cost increases.

The stock's 13.9% rally over two weeks reflects a broader shift in the energy market: oil has climbed sharply amid Middle East risks, and refinery utilization is strong while inventories remain at comfortable levels. This environment tends to support refiner earnings when demand holds steady, even as crude gets pricier.
